newsitem.title: USA: Quick & Reilly results up in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Quick & Reilly results up in second quarter.

text.p: The Quick & Reilly Group Inc. Tuesday reported stronger second-quarter results, boosted by the performance of its core discount brokerage, clearing house and specialist businesses.

Net income rose 22 percent to $18.6 million, or 74 cents per share, in the quarter ended Aug. 30, from $15.3 million, or 62 cents per share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew 11 percent to $117 million from $105.3 million.
The year-ago results reflect a three-for-two stock split in October.

"The July dip in the market was a test for our retail investors, but their interest in the market continues to be strong and we are well positioned to serve their needs," said Leslie Quick, chairman and chief executive officer.

During the quarter Quick & Reilly Inc., the group's national brokerage unit, opened branches in Reno, Nev.; Jupiter, Fla.; and a second office in Las Vegas, increasing its nationwide network to 116 offices from 108 a year ago.
"We saw growing use of our electronic access and 24-hour trading services," Quick said.

Quick & Reilly's other main subsidiaries are New York-based U.S. Clearing Corp., which provides broker/dealers and banks with execution and clearing services, and JJC Specialist Corp., the second largest specialist firm on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange.
Palm Beach, Fla.-based Quick & Reilly's stock fell $1.875 to $27.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
